blocks.content: A PriorityClass assigns a numeric priority to Pods, when resources are genuinely scarce, higher-priority Pods are scheduled first, and can even evict lower-priority ones to make room.

A PriorityClass is a cluster-level object that defines a name and a numeric priority value, Pods then reference a PriorityClass by name, rather than specifying a raw number directly in every Pod spec.

blocks.alt: A named, reusable priority level, referenced by Pods

blocks.content:
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata:
  name: high-priority
value: 1000000
globalDefault: false

blocks.content: When the scheduler has several unscheduled Pods competing for limited capacity, it considers priority, Pods referencing a higher-priority PriorityClass are considered for scheduling ahead of lower-priority ones.

blocks.alt: Priority determines who goes first when capacity is genuinely limited

blocks.content: This goes beyond just scheduling order, if a high-priority Pod cannot be placed anywhere due to insufficient capacity, Kubernetes can actually evict a lower-priority Pod to free up room for it, a real, consequential mechanism, not just a queue-ordering hint.

blocks.alt: A genuinely disruptive mechanism, not just a scheduling suggestion

blocks.content: 4. System-Critical Workloads Use Very High Priorities
blocks.text: 4. System-Critical Workloads Use Very High Priorities

blocks.content: Kubernetes itself defines built-in, very high priority classes for genuinely critical system components, ensuring core cluster functionality is never starved out by ordinary application workloads competing for the same resources.

blocks.alt: Reserved, very high priority for the components the cluster itself depends on

blocks.content: A production-critical service might reference a custom, elevated PriorityClass, ensuring it is scheduled ahead of, and protected from being preempted by, less critical batch workloads sharing the same cluster.

blocks.alt: A critical service, deliberately protected ahead of less important workloads

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: A PriorityClass assigns Pods a named priority level, higher priority means scheduled first when resources are scarce.
Preemption is the real, consequential part, a high-priority Pod can actually evict a lower-priority one to make room, not just wait patiently in a queue.
